title: Introduction to Strong and Weak Acids and Bases

children.text: The strengths of Brønsted-Lowry acids and bases in aqueous solutions are determined by their ionization constants. Strong acids ionize completely in water, while weak acids only partially ionize. Similarly, strong bases fully react with water to form hydroxide ions, whereas weak bases produce fewer hydroxide ions.

Polyprotic acids, which contain more than one ionizable proton, ionize in steps with significantly different ionization constants for each proton. This stepwise ionization helps simplify the calculation of ion concentrations in solutions.

When an acid reacts with a  base, they form a salt and water and ‘neutralize’ each other. Solutions containing salts or hydrated metal ions may be acidic, basic, or neutral, depending on the composition of the salt. We can determine the pH via calculations involving equilibrium constants, or by direct measurement. Acid strength varies across the periodic table: for binary acids (HX), it generally increases from left to right across a period and down a group. Oxyacid strength increases with higher oxidation numbers and greater electronegativity of the central element.
